whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Tableau Server Administrator exam?

personas.label: IT administrators
personas.description: You deploy, configure, and maintain Tableau Server or Tableau Cloud for an organization.

personas.label: Identity and system administrators
personas.description: You manage users, SAML or directory authentication, and security settings for Tableau Server.

personas.label: Platform operations teams
personas.description: You monitor service health, schedule extracts, investigate failures, and manage backup and recovery.

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the Tableau Server Administrator exam?
examDifficulty.summary: This exam tests Tableau administration, including TSM commands, server processes, and troubleshooting. Hands-on experience with server operations is important; reading documentation alone may leave gaps.
bullets: 50 scored questions in 90 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
64% to pass, which is 32 correct answers out of 50.
TSM knowledge. Review configuration, backup, restore, and maintenance operations.
Practical administration. Practise refresh troubleshooting, authentication setup, and Admin Views.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Before booking, practise common TSM operations, troubleshoot a failed extract refresh, configure SAML SSO, and read Admin Views without relying on step-by-step notes.

examFormat.heading: Tableau Server Administrator exam format
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test centre. Questions describe administrative tasks and server issues:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenarios may cover failed refreshes, slow dashboards, authentication errors, or server maintenance and ask for the right diagnostic or corrective action.
bestWayToPass: Practise TSM: Review status, configuration, restart, backup, and restore commands.
Learn server processes: Know the roles of VizQL, Backgrounder, Data Server, and Repository, and which logs help diagnose failures.
Review authentication: Study SAML, directory synchronization, OpenID Connect, and Kerberos, plus common troubleshooting steps.
Use Admin Views: Practise Background Tasks, Traffic to Views, and Stats for Space Used to monitor the platform.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers Tableau Server administration, including installation, configuration, process architecture, user and content management, authentication, monitoring, maintenance, and troubleshooting. The exam is 50 scored questions in 90 minutes, with a 64% pass mark, weighted towards Administration (36%) and Install & Configure (26%).

keyConcepts.h2: Tableau Server Administrator: concepts to review

blocks.heading: Server architecture and processes
blocks.body: Tableau Server uses processes that can run on one or more nodes. VizQL renders views; Application Server handles web requests and API calls; Data Server manages data connections and caching; Backgrounder runs tasks such as refreshes and subscriptions; Data Engine stores and queries Hyper extracts; and Repository (PostgreSQL) stores users, content, and workgroup metadata. A single-node installation runs processes on one machine; a multi-node cluster distributes them for scale and resilience.

blocks.heading: Installation, configuration, and TSM
blocks.body: Tableau Services Manager (TSM) provides command-line and web-based administration for Tableau Server. TSM commands change configuration and manage backups and restores. The web interface supports common administrative tasks. Installation requires a supported server, an administrator account, and a product key. Initial setup includes an administrator, authentication mode, and SSL/TLS certificates as needed. Identity stores can be local, Active Directory, or LDAP.

blocks.heading: Users and licenses
blocks.body: Site roles define user capabilities: Creator users can create and publish; Explorers can interact and have limited editing; Viewers can view content. License limits depend on the license agreement. Active Directory group synchronization can automate user provisioning and map groups to site roles. Users may belong to multiple sites with different roles. Monitor licence use and reports to stay within the organization’s entitlements.

blocks.heading: Projects, content, and permissions
blocks.body: Projects organize workbooks, data sources, and flows in a hierarchy. Permission capabilities include View, Download, Edit, Publish, Connect, Move, and Delete. Permissions may be allowed, denied, or inherited from a project. Child projects normally inherit from their parent unless configured otherwise. Locked permissions enforce the project’s permission model and prevent content owners from changing permissions on individual items. Design the project structure around governance and business needs.

blocks.heading: Monitoring and troubleshooting
blocks.body: Admin Views show server activity such as background tasks, user activity, traffic to views, and disk use. TSM jobs commands help manage background work. Tableau Server logs provide detail about process activity and can help investigate refresh, rendering, and authentication issues. The repository can support advanced usage analysis. Monitor refresh outcomes and investigate common causes such as credentials, network problems, and query timeouts.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Tableau Server Administrator exam
scenarioTips.intro: Review installation, configuration, performance monitoring, and troubleshooting. Practise TSM, backup and restore, and user management at scale.

blocks.heading: Use TSM confidently
blocks.body: Practise status, configuration, restart, backup, restore, and site export or import commands.

blocks.heading: Manage users and content
blocks.body: Review local and directory users, site roles, groups, CSV imports, project permissions, and site limits.

blocks.heading: Monitor platform activity
blocks.body: Use Admin Views for background tasks, space use, and view traffic. Learn when the Resource Monitoring Tool and repository data help.

blocks.heading: Plan backup and recovery
blocks.body: Know what a TSM backup contains and how to restore it, including what to do after a node failure.

blocks.heading: Configure authentication
blocks.body: Study local, Active Directory or LDAP, SAML SSO, OpenID Connect, and Kerberos, including their effects on provisioning and sessions.

sampleQuestions.question: Which command-line tool manages Tableau Server settings and services?
sampleQuestions.explanation: TSM manages Tableau Server configuration, topology, and service operations.
whyWrong: psql is a PostgreSQL client, not Tableau’s supported server administration tool.
Tableau Desktop is used to author workbooks.
tabcmd automates content actions such as publishing or exporting.

sampleQuestions.question: Which tool can script publishing a workbook or exporting a view to PDF?
sampleQuestions.explanation: tabcmd supports scripted content operations such as publishing and exporting views.
whyWrong: TSM configures and manages the Tableau Server platform.
Administrators manage tasks through supported interfaces rather than invoking a process directly.
Direct repository writes are not a supported way to manage content.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Tableau Server process runs scheduled extract refreshes and subscriptions?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Backgrounder executes scheduled work such as extract refreshes and subscription delivery.
whyWrong: VizQL renders views for interactive use.
Repository stores metadata rather than running scheduled jobs.
Gateway routes incoming requests.

sampleQuestions.question: Dashboards are slow during interactive use, but scheduled refreshes finish normally. Which process should the administrator investigate first?
sampleQuestions.explanation: VizQL renders interactive views, while refresh jobs are already completing normally.
whyWrong: Backgrounder handles the scheduled jobs that are working as expected.
TSM Controller manages administration, not view rendering.
Licensing affects access rather than dashboard rendering speed.

sampleQuestions.question: Extract refreshes are delayed, but interactive performance is fine. What is a suitable response?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The symptom points to Backgrounder capacity or schedule contention rather than interactive rendering.
whyWrong: VizQL handles interactive views, which are not slow here.
Authentication is unrelated to refresh queue length.
Site count alone does not determine refresh throughput.

sampleQuestions.question: A user must publish workbooks and manage permissions for selected projects, but should not administer the whole site. What access fits?
options: Server Administrator role for the entire Tableau installation
Publishing role plus project leader rights
No license, with group access only
sampleQuestions.explanation: The site role grants publishing capability, and project leader rights apply to the specified projects.
whyWrong: Server Administrator grants broad control of the installation.
A user needs an appropriate license to sign in and publish.
Viewers cannot publish or manage project permissions.

sampleQuestions.question: What happens when project permissions are locked?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Locked permissions enforce the project’s model on its content and prevent item-level permission changes.
whyWrong: Visibility still depends on the configured permissions.
Refresh scheduling is not changed by permission locking.
The lock does not change every user’s site role.

sampleQuestions.question: Which TSM command creates a full server backup for recovery?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The maintenance backup operation creates a backup archive containing server data needed for recovery.
whyWrong: tabcmd get retrieves content rather than creating a server backup.
tsm status reports process and service state.
Cleanup removes logs and temporary files; it does not create a backup.

sampleQuestions.question: What does `tsm maintenance cleanup` do?
options: Changes site roles for all users
Removes old logs and temporary files
sampleQuestions.explanation: Cleanup frees disk space by removing older logs and temporary files.
whyWrong: Use a backup command to create recovery data.
Search-index maintenance is a separate task.
Site roles are managed through user administration tools.

sampleQuestions.question: Users can reach the sign-in page, but authentication fails after an external identity provider was configured. What should be checked first?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A sign-in failure after identity-provider configuration points to the authentication settings or certificate trust.
whyWrong: Backgrounder processes scheduled jobs, not sign-in.
Workbook permissions apply after a user authenticates.
Refresh schedules do not control authentication.

sampleQuestions.question: Why create multiple sites on one Tableau Server installation?
options: To back up the same content automatically
To increase refresh throughput per node
Separate user and content areas by site
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sites provide separate content and user areas within a single Tableau Server installation.
whyWrong: Sites are not a backup mechanism.
Refresh throughput depends on process capacity and scheduling.
Authentication settings are not enabled by creating multiple sites.

sampleQuestions.question: How does Tableau licensing relate to site roles?
options: Every role uses the same license tier
Viewers do not need a license
sampleQuestions.explanation: The user’s site role determines the license tier they consume, subject to the organization’s license agreement.
whyWrong: Different roles can require different license tiers.
Viewers require a Viewer license.
Licenses are not assigned to projects.

sampleQuestions.question: Where can an administrator review which views are used least often?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Administrative views provide usage and content activity data for planning cleanup.
whyWrong: Workbook XML defines content rather than reporting its usage.
Gateway logs are not a convenient usage summary.
Configuration files describe setup, not view activity.

sampleQuestions.question: A published data source needs to refresh on schedule without a user signed in. What should be configured?
options: A new site for that data source
Store credentials with the data source
A higher role for all viewers
sampleQuestions.explanation: Embedded credentials allow scheduled refreshes to authenticate when no user is present.
whyWrong: Creating a site does not provide a database login.
A higher Tableau site role does not authenticate to the source database.
A prompt cannot be answered when no user is present.

sampleQuestions.question: A production configuration change requires a service restart. What should the administrator do first?
options: Apply the change during peak traffic
Back up, then use a maintenance window
Change all users to the Viewer role
sampleQuestions.explanation: A planned maintenance window reduces disruption, and a backup provides a recovery point before the change.
whyWrong: Restarting during peak use creates avoidable disruption.
Deleting workbooks is unrelated to configuration changes.
Changing roles does not reduce the effect of a service restart.
